scope: Synthetic FP32 projection fixtures; not real-model or HTTP serving measurements.

paired_protocol.variant_order: before/after on even trials, after/before on odd trials
paired_protocol.reference: originalFP32Dispatch copies the baseline FP32 reduction body into the test binary; it is not a second full model implementation.
paired_protocol.validation: Exact finite FP32 output bits checked before and after timing in every case. Current standalone fallback, inline execution and fixed workers run in the same process as their reference.
paired_protocol.allocation_measurement: testing.AllocsPerRun(20) after warmup; Go runs this measurement at GOMAXPROCS=1. Timed pairs use GOMAXPROCS=4.

generation_protocol.method: Package-renamed complete baseline and candidate runtimes execute in one process. Three fresh processes, 24 alternating-order pairs per case, identical seed-19 synthetic models. Fixed-step tokenizer disables EOS. Every completion JSON matches; serialization is outside timing. Interface adapters add common boxing overhead inside timing.
generation_protocol.interpretation: Across-process medians of paired ratios are approximately within -1.5% to +1.3% for all five conditions. Individual process medians include +3.0%. This supports allocation-focused adoption, not a claim of universal latency improvement.
generation_protocol.separate_process_caveat: ABBA process-level timing includes slower prefill observations (about 7-9%) and larger excursions in unchanged quantized controls. Those samples are retained, not reclassified as improvements; the paired full-runtime experiment was added to reduce cross-process clock/scheduling confounding.

hypotheses.name: caller participates in worker computation
hypotheses.disposition: Not selected: small synthetic kernels regressed and larger kernels did not establish a general benefit.

hypotheses.name: reduce parallelism for small projections
hypotheses.disposition: Not selected: worker-width exploration showed slower serial execution for the measured 256-to-704 projection shapes. Existing thresholds unchanged.

hypotheses.name: send a typed FP32 job through the shared worker mailbox
hypotheses.disposition: Rejected: lower allocations but unfavorable timing, including quantized controls. Full negative comparison is fp32-dispatch-20261106.json.

hypotheses.name: cache one FP32 callback on the request-owned executor
hypotheses.disposition: Promising for allocations, but the first extracted kernel with many scalar/slice arguments regressed the large single-row case in paired timing.

hypotheses.name: cached callback with a pointer-based FP32 invocation descriptor
hypotheses.disposition: Selected as an allocation reduction, with unchanged arithmetic and worker thresholds. Inline kernels bypass dispatch; shared mailbox layout is unchanged. One callback is allocated at executor startup, and invocation references are cleared after every joined kernel.

conclusions: Warm executor-owned FP32 kernels allocate zero objects per invocation, versus one previously. The default regression test verifies worker counts 1, 2 and 4 and non-tile-aligned dimensions.
Three paired processes preserve this allocation result across all owned-executor cases; nil fallback keeps its allocation count rather than promising zero allocations.
Median paired ratios across the three processes for each condition are approximately within -2.2% to +2.0%. Individual process medians include a +5.7% case; all raw samples are retained.

No uniform latency speedup, peak RSS decrease, lower GC frequency, real-model throughput gain or quantized-kernel speedup is established. Startup incurs one cached callback allocation and bounded descriptor storage.
reproduction: Repeat in three fresh processes; use taskset -c 0-3 only on a compatible Linux CPU topology. On other platforms omit taskset and record the host.
